scores.evidence: POSIX `rename` silently replaces an existing target. Case-only renames behave differently across filesystems.
scores.rationale: Technical claims are accurate and precise throughout, including subtle areas (POSIX rename semantics, Windows no-overwrite behavior, EXIF sentinel values, DateTime being editor-overwritten, renameat2 NOREPLACE).

scores.evidence: Rename a folder of up to about 10,000 photos so that sorting by name puts them in capture order.
scores.rationale: Solves exactly the stated problem, resolves ambiguities with stated defaults and open questions, and explicitly justifies every exclusion (videos, recursion, GUI).

scores.evidence: The Planner is a pure function and holds all the decision logic. Only the Executor changes the filesystem
scores.rationale: Clean single-writer pipeline with explicit data ownership per component; decisions (no-overwrite, occupied-name rule, journal) are honored consistently across every section.

scores.evidence: Spike A (1 day, time-boxed): Does `exifread` read `DateTimeOriginal`/`SubSecTimeOriginal` for ≥99.5% of the user's real files
scores.rationale: Riskiest assumptions (library coverage, filesystem semantics) are spiked before commitment, with checkable criteria, property tests, fault injection, SHA-256 invariants and explicit plan-change triggers.

scores.evidence: Every target above is an assumption until you confirm it.
scores.rationale: Assumptions table states each assumption, its impact if wrong, and how/when it is validated; all numeric targets are explicitly labeled provisional.

scores.evidence: The disk is pulled out at operation 400 of 812... Running `undo` instead restores the 400 renamed files
scores.rationale: Covers domain-specific failures (interrupted runs, corrupt EXIF, burst collisions, case-insensitive clashes, check-then-rename race, split pairs) with concrete detection, containment and recovery.

scores.evidence: Support means the README, the `--verbose` output and the journal file. Releases are tagged on PyPI (M3).
scores.rationale: Operations are sized correctly to a single-user CLI: 3-OS CI, versioned journal, pipx version pinning for rollback, and user-side rollout guidance (copy folder first).
Correctly identifies engineering time as the only cost, gives ranged labeled estimates per milestone, and weighs build-vs-buy trade-offs (exifread vs ExifTool, Python vs Go).
Every key decision carries an explicit reversibility rating and revisit trigger; the hard-to-reverse ones (journal schema, language) are versioned or validated early via spikes.

scores.evidence: One Python package with a pipeline of small modules... There is no database.
scores.rationale: Simplest workable design—stdlib plus one read-only library—with every element justified, no speculative infrastructure, and explicit deferrals with triggers for growth.

scores.evidence: T2 and T3 run in parallel from day one. T4 next, then T5, T6 and T7 in parallel.
scores.rationale: Ten tasks with concrete done-when criteria, dependency-justified ordering, a named critical path, and explicit 'changes the plan if' clauses for spike outcomes.

checklist.evidence: Get the capture time from `DateTimeOriginal`, fall back to `DateTimeDigitized`, and never use `DateTime`, because editing software overwrites that field.
Rejects empty values, all-zero values, and anything that won't parse as a date... M2 adds `--fallback=mtime`, off by default, marked in the report
Name clashes get deterministic suffixes (`_1`, `_2`), and an existing file's name always counts as taken.
Dry run is the default. `--apply` is required to change anything, and it asks for confirmation.
a candidate name is taken if any file currently in the folder has it... This rules out rename chains and cycles
Every applied run writes a journal. `photo-rename undo` reverses it exactly, even after a crash partway through.
EXIF local time is used as recorded, with no time-zone conversion... Offset tags are often missing
Grouping by base name (RAW+JPEG, `.xmp`/`.aae` sidecars, Live Photo `.mov` follows its HEIC)
`YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS` with the original extension kept as is... `--format` arrives in M2

traps.evidence: Before each rename, it checks that the source still exists and that the target is free (case-insensitively)
never use `DateTime`, because editing software overwrites that field... Modified times are often copy times
Everything runs in one process with no network access... There is no database.
Reads headers only and never opens files for writing... It never writes into a photo.
Name format is `YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS` with the original extension kept as is

note: An exemplary plan: technically precise, proportionate, risk-driven, and immediately actionable, with explicit assumptions, early spikes on the real risks, and crash-safe undo semantics.
